Manek Nabi Kaasambhai vs State Of Gujarat on 4 March, 2024 
Author: Ilesh J. Vora
Bench: Ilesh J. Vora
 
 R/Cr.Ma/23159/2022 Order  DATED: 04/03/2024  
 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION (FOR QUASHING & SET ASIDE  FIR/ORDER) NO. 23159 of 2022 ==========================================================
 MANEK NABI KAASAMBHAI  Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT & ANR.
==========================================================
Appearance:
MR VICKY B MEHTA(5422) for the Applicant(s) No. 1 for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MR JAY MEHTA, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ILESH J. VORA  Date : 04/03/2024  ORAL ORDER 1. By invoking inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure Code, the applicant Manik Kasambhai, has preferred this application thereby he is seeking quashment of the FIR being CR. No.11211015220301 of 2022 registered with Dhrangadhra City Police Station District Surendranagar for the offences punishable under Section 332, 337, 186,
160, 143, 147, 148, 149, 506(2), 504 and 427 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3 of the Prevention of Damage to Public Property Act and Section 135 of the Gujarat Police Act. 
2. Brief facts emerges from the record are that the aforesaid FIR was being registered on 29.09.2022. On the day of incident, the Police Officers of the Dhrangadhra City Police Station were Manek Nabi Kaasambhai vs State Of Gujarat on 4 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10024151/
1 on patrolling in the town as there was a Navratri festivities. They NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23159/2022 ORDER DATED: 04/03/2024 undefined received the information about scuffle and commotion took place between two communities. Accordingly, the Police Officials reached and trite to calm-down the situation and on persuasion by them the one of the community peoples went from the place but the opposition party did not left the place, as a result, the Police officials was compelled to use force and in that process due to incitement of the accused and others,
they pelted the stones upon the police officials which has led to cause to injury to the Police officials. 
The people which were part of the said unlawful assembly, having armed with deadly weapon started to cause damages to vehicles of the vicinity and the other property of the society and restrained the Police officials in performing their official duties. In such circumstances, the police officials of City Police Station has lodged an FIR against 24 persons by their names and others for the offence of causing voluntarily hurt to deter public servant from his duty by act of endangering life and or personal safety of others and cause damages to the property. 
3. This Court has heard learned counsel Mr. Vicky Mehta and State counsel Mr. Mehta on advance copy. 
4. Mr. Mehta appearing for and on behalf fo the applicant has submitted that the applicant was not part of the alleged unlawful assembly and did not have participated in the offence and because of his food stall nearby this place of offence he was present there and on that count on the basis of the statement of co-accused he has been falsely arraigned in the said offence and also initially not named in the FIR. In such circumstances, he has NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23159/2022 ORDER DATED: 04/03/2024 undefined submitted that except the statement of the co-accused, no other evidence is found to prove the involvement of the applicant in the alleged offence and thus the complainant being a police officials with ulterior motive, he has been ropped in the alleged offence which about the a gross abuse of process of law.
5. In view of the aforesaid contention Mr. Mehta has submitted that when the criminal proceeding found to be malafide or otherwise an abuse of the process of law and Court, it is incumbent on the part of the High Court to protect the innocent person by exercising its inherent powers. 
6. On the other hand, learned APP Mr. Mehta, has submitted that the contentions as raised being a disputed question of fact cannot be examined at this stage as the investigation is still not completed and therefore, at this stage, powers should not exercise to thwart investigation and proceedings ought not to be scuttled at the initial stage. 
7. Having considered the contentions raised by the counsel appearing for the respective parties and on perusal of the allegations levelled against the applicant in the FIR, this Court is of the considered view that till date the investigation is not completed. The offence alleged registered against the mob and in that view of the matter when there is a charge of joining unlawful assembly armed with deadly weapon and rioting, the individual role of the person cannot be examined at this stage. 
Section 149 of the IPC says that if an offence is committed by NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23159/2022 ORDER DATED: 04/03/2024 undefined any member of unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object of that assembly or such as the members of that assembly Manek Nabi Kaasambhai vs State Of Gujarat on 4 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10024151/
2 knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object, every person, who at the time of committing of the offence is a member of the same assembly is guilty of the said offence. In the facts of the presence case, there was a mob of around 100 and more and in that view of the matter, it is difficult to lay or mention in the FIR the role of each person by the complainant. It is submitted that,
due to business of food stall near the area of place of offence, the presence of the applicant would natural and therefore, mere a fact that, person doing business in nearby place of offence is not sufficient to show that he was a member of unlawful assembly, which committed the offence. This Court is conscious about the settled position of law that mere presence does not make out a case. 
However, the facts remains that, after registration of the offence, the applicant was apprehended and presently he is on bail and till date, the chargesheet has not been filed qua the applicant herein. 
Therefore, the contention that, the applicant was being an owner of the food stall do not have any connection with the alleged commission of offence cannot be accepted at this stage as still he has not been arraigned in the chargesheet finally. In such circumstances, remedy is available to the applicant to file a discharge application in case chargesheet is filed and trial Court having all the opportunity to examine the chargesheet case papers meticulously. 
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23159/2022 ORDER DATED: 04/03/2024 undefined 8. In view of aforesaid facts and circumstances, this Court deem it not necessary to enter into disputed question of facts as raised herein and this is not a stage to decide whether there is any truth in the allegations and there is no evidence to implicate the applicant in the said crime. Hence, I am of the opinion that, this is not a fit case to exercise powers under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to quash the FIR at the initial stage and the allegations made in the complaint has to be properly investigated by the police and if power is invoked then it amount to interfering with the investigation. Therefore,
application requires to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed at the admission stage. 
9. It is made clear that the observations made are prima-facie in nature and confined to the adjudication of present application. The trial Court shall not get influenced by the said observations during the adjudication of discharge application, if any, filed by the applicant-accused. 
(ILESH J. VORA,J) TAUSIF SAIYED Manek Nabi Kaasambhai vs State Of Gujarat on 4 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10024151/
